Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Recap + next steps — Private VPC qualification

Hi Alice & Rajiv,

Thanks for the call earlier — good alignment on use case and constraints. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can qualify the right deployment mode (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC):

Summary of what we heard
- Primary concern: strict data residency and network isolation for transaction logs + audit trails.
- Procurement leans toward customer-controlled peering (they want to avoid cross-account endpoints unless required).
- Traffic profile: bursty read/write ingestion (~120 rps sustained peaks today; expect growth).
- Compliance: SOC 2 in-scope + retention/audit requirements.

Preliminary recommendation
- Private VPC (Redwood Private) looks like the best fit because it gives you control over network boundaries and KMS/HSM options.
- If Procurement insists on avoiding routing changes, we can support either PrivateLink (cross-account interface endpoint) or VPC peering — pros/cons below.

Immediate asks (action items)
1) Please complete the attached network_cidr_template.csv with the VPC/CIDR ranges, desired subnets for Redwood services (control plane vs compute), and any egress NAT requirements.
2) Confirm preference: PrivateLink (interface endpoints) or VPC peering. If unsure, note both and we’ll discuss tradeoffs in the technical deep-dive.
3) Share the contact for your infra engineer (we’ll include them in the technical deep-dive).

Attachments: network_cidr_template.csv (template), netfin_security_questionnaire.pdf (security/governance), dap_private_link_instructions.docx (how PrivateLink works on our side).

Next step
- Let’s schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive with your infra and procurement teams. I’m proposing Wed 11/11 or Thu 11/12 morning PST — what works?

Thanks — I’ll slot a tentative invite once I hear availability.

Jonas Weber
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Jonas — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- NetFin prefers PrivateLink from a security posture perspective, but procurement is pushing for VPC peering because our security team is more familiar with it. Open to either as long as we maintain strict ingress/egress controls.
- Do you provide a set of static egress IPs we can allowlist for outbound callbacks (webhooks) if we go with PrivateLink or Hosted? Procurement needs to know whether we need to add Redwood IPs to our allowlist.
- We can have our infra lead (Rajiv) join the deep-dive. He can bring our network diagrams and current peering policies.

Can you also confirm whether Dedicated capacity gives us static egress IPs or if that’s only available with Private (customer-managed) deployments?

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Park <alice@netfin.co>, Rajiv Mehta <rajiv@netfin.co>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 11:00:25 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps — Private VPC qualification

Alice — great questions. Short answers here, TL;DR at the top then detail:

TL;DR
- PrivateLink and VPC peering are both supported. We typically recommend PrivateLink when you want minimal routing changes and strong isolation; peering is fine if your procurement/security team requires it.
- Static egress IPs: for Hosted API we publish a set of egress IP ranges you can allowlist (best-effort, may change with region); Dedicated offers an option for static egress IPs via a managed NAT; Private (customer-managed) deployments running in your VPC provide control of egress IPs entirely to you (you manage NAT/GW).

Details
- PrivateLink (interface endpoints): Pros = cross-account isolation, no peering routes needed, easier to restrict to specific subnets. Cons = requires interface endpoints and security group rules on your side; some procurement teams see it as 3rd-party endpoint.
- VPC peering: Pros = direct routing, familiar to some ops teams. Cons = route table changes and potential overlap issues; not ideal if you want strict separation between services.

Allowlist guidance
- If you choose PrivateLink (Redwood-hosted interface): you will need to allowlist our interface endpoint DNS + any outbound IPs for callbacks. We can provide a small set of stable IP ranges for the planned region — I’ve attached dap_private_link_instructions.docx which includes the typical CIDR ranges and setup steps.
- If you choose Dedicated with managed NAT: we can allocate a static NAT IP (single egress IP or small pool).
- If you choose Private (deployed into your VPC): your infra controls egress; Redwood does not require outbound IP exceptions because traffic remains in your VPC unless you explicitly route egress.

Next step: please populate network_cidr_template.csv with your VPC/CIDR info and indicate whether you prefer PrivateLink or peering. I’ll then have Marissa and Monica draft a technical agenda for the deep-dive.

Attachments: dap_private_link_instructions.docx, netfin_security_questionnaire.pdf

Best,
Jonas
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

Please go ahead and book the technical deep-dive Thursday 11/12 at 1pm PST. Include Marissa and Monica — they’ll lead the implementation discussion. Also cc our procurement lead (procurement@netfin.co) on any contract/egress IP docs.

Thanks,
